business_scope.primary_industry_name: C-Suite Executive Search and Specialist Tech Headhunting

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic/Napoleonic tradition; statutory primacy; no binding stare decisis).
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EEA Agreement (1994) granting free establishment and cross-border services under TFEU Articles 49 and 56.

Double Taxation Treaties with over 80 jurisdictions, including Germany, France, the Netherlands and the Luxembourg–United States income tax treaty (signed 1996, entered into force 2000, amended by protocol 2009).
BLEU–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 6 June 2005, entered into force 1 May 2009).
BLEU–Hong Kong Investment Protection and Promotion Agreement (in force since 2014).
EU–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) investment provisions (provisionally in force).

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Luxembourg AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (notably by the Law of 25 March 2020 and the 2023 implementing legislation following the CJEU rulings in joined cases C-37/20 and C-601/20); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 22 October 2019 on the RBE; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended by the Law of 12 July 2013 introducing the SCSp; CSSF Regulation 12-02 and CSSF Circulars 18/679 and 18/698.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity document of each individual UBO (general partner and limited partners holding 25% or more)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO country of residence or issuing passport authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization if the origin country is not an Apostille Convention member)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or corporate extract for any corporate UBO or corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign commercial registry or competent companies registrar
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague origins)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney granted to Luxembourg counsel and/or licensed domiciliation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the grantor country of residence or Luxembourg notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference or account conduct letter for the founding general partner (KYC and provenance of funds)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relationship bank or correspondent financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostilled or consularly legalized, or authenticated through the issuing bank legalization department

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution and constitutional documents of any corporate participant authorizing the Luxembourg SCSp participation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or board of the foreign corporate participant

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, the general partner and commercial beneficiaries against (i) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, (ii) UN Security Council sanctions, and (iii) the Luxembourg national PEP database prior to RBE filing and bank onboarding. Enhanced due diligence is applied to non-EU resident UBOs and to any politically exposed person, consistent with CSSF Circular 18/679 risk-based CDD requirements. As standard market practice for USD-denominated retainer wires, OFAC SDN screening is also performed; any positive hit must be escalated to the AML responsible officer within 24 hours.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); online pre-incorporation name clearance via the LBR Guichet unique at www.lbr.lu.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Official registry language is French; proposed names must be submitted in Latin script. Non-Latin script names (e.g., Chinese or Cyrillic) must be transliterated into Latin characters, and that transliteration becomes the registered name; the transliteration must not be deceptive or phonetically confusing. The registered name of an SCSp must be followed or preceded by the statutory suffix SCSp (Société en commandite spéciale).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words suggesting a regulated financial institution without prior ministerial consent: banque, assurance, fonds, OPCVM, SICAV, fiduciaire, trust.
Words suggesting a state or public body: Administration, Ministère, État, Chambre, Commission (unless corporate form clearly excludes public association).
Regulated liberal professions requiring professional chamber approval: avocat, notaire, expert-comptable, réviseur d'entreprises, agent immobilier.
The token Luxembourg in the company name requires documentary proof of authorization from the Ministry of the Economy or other competent authority.
Words contrary to public policy (ordre public) or likely to mislead the public as to the object, nationality or liability structure of the partnership.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If LBR rejects the proposed name, the applicant receives a motivated refusal. Remedy path: (1) re-file a corrected name application through the LBR Guichet unique without pecuniary penalty; (2) request a written de novo review by the LBR legal department attaching justification; (3) within three months of notification, lodge an administrative appeal with the Tribunal Administratif de Luxembourg, with the possibility of interim suspension relief. Name reservations are valid for 60 days; one prolongation of 60 days may be requested before expiry upon payment of the applicable LBR tariff.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not acceptable as a standalone solution: the SCSp must maintain a verifiable physical registered office in Luxembourg (Article 158 of the Law of 10 August 1915). A licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent may provide a commercial address, but central administration, statutory books and decision-making records must remain accessible in Luxembourg; pure mail-forwarding offices fail LBR and banking KYC substance checks. For a headhunting agency with retainer fees, substance indicators such as a Luxembourg bank account, a local general partner and local management minutes are expected.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, approximately 10% probability per year for this low-risk service business. Unannounced physical inspections are exceptional for an SCSp without regulated-license activity; however, LBR and tax authorities may request proof of registered office in response to third-party flags or on a risk-based sample.

Publication of the partnership deed in the RCS electronic collection (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: LBR publication fee schedule, short act with annexes (approximately EUR 75)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial drafting and execution of the SCSp partnership agreement with three certified copies
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market tariff for authentic acts (approximately EUR 2,000)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and/or consular legalization of four foreign KYC and UBO documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Origin-country apostille authority (e.g., U.S. Department of State) or consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee per document (approximately USD 150 x 4)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial UBO registration in the RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutorily free of charge for the first filing (electronic register)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RBE filing support, UBO certificate and compliance folder preparation
Business establishment authorization (autorisation d'établissement) application fee
Registered office domiciliation service at a licensed Luxembourg provider (year 1)
AML/KYC professional file: PEP and sanctions screening, UBO piercing, document verification and bank account introduction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed professional fee for pre-incorporation compliance work (market benchmark)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Professional indemnity insurance premium (year 1, market-standard for executive search)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market premium based on headcount and revenue ceiling (approximately EUR 1,000)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translations (French, German, English) of corporate documents, IDs and powers of attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator or certified translation bureau

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and legalization of the power of attorney to Luxembourg counsel

stage_2.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Directorate General for SMEs (Direction générale des classes moyennes) through the Single Permit Desk (Guichet unique / eLuxembourg portal)
stage_2.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Authorization) for commercial service providers; supplemented by NACE/ISIC activity coding (ISIC 7830 / NACE 78.30 – Other human resources provision)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C – Non-classified office activity; exempt from full EIA; no environmental impact assessment report required for a headhunting agency operating from a commercial office lease
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process discharge; compliance with the Grand-Ducal Regulation on waste management (household office waste), municipal wastewater connection standards, and EU indoor VOC/air quality limits applicable to office fit-outs; EED energy-efficiency obligations for the leased premises apply.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; central administrative portal is MyGuichet.lu / Guichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must first register with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through MyGuichet.lu, obtaining the national business registration identification number (matricule). Thereafter, the entity files a VAT registration application with the AEDT via the same portal. Once processed, the AEDT issues a Luxembourg VAT identification number in the format LU + 8 digits. Non-EU established foreign entities may be required to appoint a Luxembourg fiscal representative for VAT purposes. All tax IDs are administered electronically; no physical presence is prerequisite for obtaining the TIN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: An SCSp (Société en Commandite Spéciale) is generally fiscally transparent under Luxembourg tax law unless it validly elects to be treated as a taxable entity for corporation income tax purposes (option pour le régime des sociétés). Additional elections may apply under Luxembourg's implementation of EU ATAD hybrid mismatch rules, enabling alignment of tax characterization with foreign jurisdictions. The partnership agreement can also contain internal structures supporting transparent or opaque treatment, subject to anti-abuse review.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Luxembourg-established small businesses may benefit from the €35,000 annual turnover exemption (excluding VAT) and thus avoid mandatory registration until this threshold is exceeded. Non-established foreign suppliers are required to register from their first taxable transaction in Luxembourg, irrespective of turnover. Cross-border B2C distance sales of goods become subject to Luxembourg VAT when the supplier's EU-wide distance sales exceed €10,000 annually.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg mandates electronic invoicing for B2G transactions through the PEPPOL network under the eDPI law. There is no general real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control obligation for B2B invoices. For private sector invoices, submission is not clearance-based; invoices must contain the VAT-compliant data fields. E-invoicing may also be used voluntarily in addition to standard paper or PDF invoicing.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to destinations outside the EU qualify for the 0% VAT rate provided the goods physically leave Luxembourg/EU territory within the statutory period (generally 3 months for exports; evidence of removal must be retained). Intra-Community supplies to a customer holding a valid EU VAT identification number also qualify for 0% where transport to another EU member state is proven. For executive search and headhunting services supplied to a non-resident business customer, the place of supply is the customer's country, thereby falling outside Luxembourg VAT (not strictly zero-rating but effectively unprotected from Luxembourg VAT). All zero-rating claims require substantive documentary proof and commercial substance.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg's VAT authority conducts risk-based audits focusing on export substantiation, particularly for service exporters and high-volume goods exporters. Missing or inadequate evidence may result in retrospective VAT reassessment at the standard rate, denial of refunds, and clawback of previously zero-rated outputs. Administrative penalties for false declarations or unjustified zero-rating can exceed €100,000 and reach up to 10% of the tax evaded; serious cases attract criminal sanctions and personal liability of directors or representatives. Default interest accrues monthly on unremitted VAT until full repayment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), Eurosystem member; banking, payment institution, and e-money institution prudential supervision and AML/CFT oversight are exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg uses the euro and maintains zero exchange controls; Article 63 TFEU secures free movement of capital within the EU and vis-à-vis third countries, so current-account retainer fees and capital-account contributions to an SCSp are fully convertible and remittable without prior state authorisation. In practice, the counterparty bank applies its own sanction/KYC permissioning; the tax-transparent SCSp passes profits to partners with no withholding for EU-resident partners and reduced rates under Luxembourg double-tax treaties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender, retention period, or conversion ratio applies to export or retainer proceeds in Luxembourg. Foreign-currency headhunting fees may remain as USD/GBP balances; the only administrative duty is indirect: the custodial bank files BCL balance-of-payments statistics for the SCSp's cross-border direct investment and service flows, so the treasury should supply invoice and capital-call references to classify each credit.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Multi-currency + SEPA Clearing Rails

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / EUR + Payroll and VAT settlement
Capital Escrow Account / Retainer segregation sub-ledger

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High viability for collection of low-value retainer wires and disbursement to overseas sub-agents using Wise Europe SA (Belgian EMI licensed by the NBB and passported into Luxembourg under Directive 2009/110/EC) or a CSSF-licensed local EMI such as Paynovate S.A. Legal constraints: EMI balances are safeguarded rather than guaranteed by the Luxembourg deposit guarantee fund (FGDL), EMIs cannot extend credit, and the SCSp must appoint its general partner (gérant) or a mandated manager to sign the EMI mandate; EUR payments above EUR 100,000 should be settled through the principal Luxembourg bank via TARGET2 rather than through the EMI.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg tier-1 banks allow hybrid onboarding: the first KYC interview is by video conference or telephone with the compliance officer, and physical appearance is waived when the SCSp holds a Luxembourg registered office, a notarised partnership agreement, and current RCSL extracts. For an SCSp without legal personality, the general partner must sign in its own name and for the partnership, and a one-time in-person specimen signature at the bank, a notary, or a Luxembourg diplomatic post is common; EEA EMIs, including Wise, accept fully remote onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp has no legal personality and no beneficial-owner register (RBE) extract
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised partnership agreement; certificate of RCSL registration (Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register) with RBE extract under the Law of 13 January 2019; signed general partner resolution; video KYC minutes; CSSF Circular 20/744-compliant risk assessment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Headhunting classified as a regulated gatekeeper profession with third-party funds and unusually high client deposits
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ministry of Labour and Economy operating authorisation (autorisation d'établissement); compliance manual and AML/CFT policies; signed client placement pipeline; tax residence certificate; list of existing retainer contracts and expected monthly fee profile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injections into a zero-minimum-capital SCSp exceed revenue expectations or show circular funding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital call notices (appels de fonds) signed by the general partner; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth declarations of each contributor; bank reference letters; partnership ledger entries; proforma commission invoices matching the treasury forecast.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wires to high-risk third countries for candidate relocation or sub-agent commission
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EU Regulation 269/2014 sanctions screening certificates; negative-news and PEP checks; export-of-services compliance letter; remuneration schedule in the sub-agent agreement; per-transaction invoice with date, service description, and VAT references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through structure obscures the identity of ultimate beneficial owners or a partner is a PEP
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UBO table applying the 25% threshold; PEP source-of-funds declaration; chain-of-control chart; attestation that clients are non-sanctioned and that services exclude defence, crypto, or extractive sectors; enhanced due-diligence file updated within 10 working days per CSSF expectation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: EU/EEA partner contributions: SEPA Credit Transfer using the EUR IBAN with unstructured remittance reference 'APPORT EN CAPITAL - CALL N'; non-EEA contributions: SWIFT MT103 with field 70 containing the capital-call reference and field 77B showing applicant and beneficiary RCSL codes, together with a pre-alert to the receiving banker attaching the signed capital-call notice and contributor tax-residence certificate; the bank books the flow as equity under BCL balance-of-payments classification and no BCL approval is required; institutional capital above EUR 100,000 should bypass the EMI channel and use the principal correspondent bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EUR operating expenses, sub-agent commissions, payroll, and VAT obligations are cleared via SEPA Credit Transfer with full invoice and VAT references; non-EUR settlements (USD/GBP/CHF) use SWIFT MT103 with field 70 referencing the invoice and the Luxembourg VAT number, routed through the bank's correspondent network (typically via BGL or Société Générale US/UK correspondents); documentary collections and commercial letters of credit are permitted but unnecessary for intangible placement services, so the treasury uses an escrow sub-account at BIL for milestone-based retainers and Wise B2B local rails for small disbursements; each payment must satisfy deductibility documentation under Luxembourg income-tax law.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD and EUR/GBP outright forwards (1-12 months) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with CSA, classified as non-financial-counterparty trades below the EMIR clearing threshold, with reporting delegated to the counterparty bank.
EUR/USD and EUR/GBP foreign-exchange swaps (spot/forward and tom-next) used to fund multi-currency retainer receivables and to manage the SCSp's operating liquidity buffer.
European-style EUR/USD and EUR/CHF options and zero-premium collars, covered strictly by underlying placement-fee exposure, with uncovered speculative option trading prohibited by treasury policy.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in USD/CNY contracted through the bank's offshore CNH desk only where a Shanghai or Hong Kong client cannot obtain deliverable CNY hedging, documented on actual invoice exposure and supported by the relevant placement contracts.

Cross-currency basis swaps (EUR/USD) reserved for single-client USD placements above EUR 1 million, executed on a back-to-back basis with the confirmed client invoice and marked to market monthly; hedging limits must be ratified by the general partner's annual treasury resolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts (Comptes Annuels) for the SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approval required within 6 months after financial year-end; deposit at RCS within 1 month after approval. Calendar-year SCSp: approve by 30 June, file by 30 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine of EUR 50 to EUR 60,000 (approx. USD 54 to 65,000) per defaulting manager under Article 19 of the RCS Law; LBR penalty notices and public prosecutor enforcement; administrative strike-off does not exist in Luxembourg, but persistent non-filing may trigger judicial dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Confirmation (Confirmation des Beneficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 calendar days following each anniversary of the date of the SCSp's initial RBE registration (Article 16, Law of 13 January 2019)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine of EUR 500 to EUR 25,000 (approx. USD 540 to 27,100) and/or imprisonment of 6 months to 3 years for wilful false or omitted UBO data; LBR may block further RCS filings; administrative strike-off does not exist in Luxembourg

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal Business Tax Return (Impôt Commercial Communal - IFC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) and the competent commune
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Standard deadline of 31 December of the year following the tax year for calendar-year filers (e.g., FY 2025 return due by 31 December 2026); extensions granted upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly delay interest of 0.6% on unpaid IFC assessments; administrative fines after formal reminders; enforced collection by ACD; administrative strike-off does not exist in Luxembourg

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a Luxembourg-approved statutory auditor (reviseur d'entreprises agree) only where the SCSp exceeds two of three size tests at the balance-sheet date: total balance sheet above EUR 6,000,000; net turnover above EUR 12,000,000; average workforce above 50 employees. Below these thresholds the SCSp is audit-exempt under the small-company regime of the Law of 19 December 2002
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on the RCS and Annual Accounts, as amended; IFRS permitted as an alternative for non-listed entities; accounts expressed in EUR

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must file, once per calendar year, an electronic confirmation to the RBE within 15 days of the anniversary of its RBE registration confirming that the UBO data remain accurate. Any transfer of partnership interests or change in percentage of economic ownership must first be recorded in the statutory register of partners and filed as an RBE update before the annual confirmation is submitted. The LBR issues automatic prompts and flags non-compliant entities
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Partners) - registre des associes recording interest transfers
Register of Directors (General Partner and its appointed managers)
Minute Book of Partners' Meetings and Written Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,200 to US$3,000 per year (typical Luxembourg domiciliation agent fee including registered office, mail handling and RCS/RBE filing assistance)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$4,500 to US$9,500 per year (typical certified audit fee for a small to medium-size service entity under Lux GAAP; not applicable where the SCSp remains below the statutory audit thresholds)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The SCSp itself is fiscally transparent and does not bear Luxembourg corporate income tax. Corporate partners are subject to the aggregate 24.94% rate (17% CIT plus 7% solidarity surcharge plus 6.75% municipal business tax in Luxembourg City). Preferential reliefs include the participation exemption (qualifying dividends and capital gains are tax-exempt) and the IP box regime providing an 80% exemption on qualifying IP-derived income. Tax losses of a corporate partner can be carried forward indefinitely, although offsetting is limited under the minimum taxation rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 670 (annual declaration of partners) and annual accounts filed through MyGuichet.lu; the SCSp is not required to file a CIT return due to transparency.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the end of the financial year; for calendar-year entities, this is typically 30 June of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification details of the SCSp, registered office, and legal form.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners are identified by name, address, and tax residence country.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names and capital contributions of the general partner and all limited partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate each non-resident partner's share percentage and capital contribution in EUR.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of taxable income/loss for the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate Luxembourg-source executive search and headhunting fees to each partner according to the partnership agreement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing with the Luxembourg trade registry (RCS) triggers fines up to EUR 2,000. A missing partner declaration may result in ex officio assessment and a 10% increase of the assessed tax, plus monthly late interest of 7% per annum.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 620 (Corporate Income Tax Return) for corporate partners; filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu / e-SITE tax portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by 31 December of the year following the fiscal year-end for calendar-year taxpayers, unless a filing extension is granted. Quarterly instalment payments are required for normal CIT assessments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Share of taxable income allocated from the SCSp during the tax year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partner reports its Luxembourg-source allocated share and claims DTA relief or foreign tax credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions attributable to the headhunting activity, including retainer fees, payroll, and overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses economically connected with the Luxembourg-source income are deductible unless a PE exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation exemption claimed on qualifying dividends and capital gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach evidence of shareholding percentage and holding period; non-resident partner must meet the same conditions under Luxembourg law.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing automatically increases tax due by 10%; repeated offences can raise the increase to 25% and trigger a formal penalty up to EUR 250,000. Interest accrues at 7% per annum on late payments.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% standard Luxembourg dividend withholding tax; 0% where the participation exemption is satisfied. For SCSp, profit distributions to partners are generally not subject to withholding tax because the partnership is fiscally transparent.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the beneficial owner must file Luxembourg Form 105 (or Form 106 for refunds) with the direct tax administration before or after the distribution, attaching the tax residency certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, a statement of beneficial ownership, and evidence of the participation percentage and holding period. The Luxembourg tax authorities process the claim administratively and may issue an advance exemption order.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law imposes 0% withholding tax on outbound interest and royalties paid to non-residents, with no treaty override required. The statutory rate is zero; certain payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions or in abuse cases may be recharacterised.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required where intra-group services exceed EUR 150,000, goods transactions exceed EUR 1,000,000, financial transactions exceed EUR 1,000,000, or intangible transactions exceed EUR 500,000. Master File required for a multinational group with consolidated turnover above EUR 50,000,000 and local intragroup operations above the de minimis thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies the OECD/Aligned substance requirements. An SCSp must maintain real office space, operational staff, board or partner-level decision-making, and actual headhunting activity in Luxembourg to avoid challenge under ATAD, the Luxembourg general anti-abuse rule, and treaty limitation-on-benefits clauses. Shell-company arrangements are rebutted by the tax administration and may be disregarded.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of executive search fees, omission of partner allocations, creation of fictitious invoices for candidate placement, or concealment of bank accounts receiving onboarding retainers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Luxembourg General Tax Law, tax evasion is punishable by fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years. Aggravated fiscal fraud (e.g. forgery, use of offshore shell accounts) raises the maximum penalty to EUR 1,000,000 and 10 years' imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the unlimited-liability general partner may be held personally liable for unpaid tax, social security contributions, and conviction-secured civil damages. Travel bans, seizure of assets, and extradition arrangements can apply in cross-border cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SCSp as a booking vehicle for international headhunting commissions without Luxembourg clients, employees, office premises, or substantive decision-making, thereby claiming treaty benefits improperly.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation of transactions, denial of treaty benefits, and imposition of transfer pricing adjustments. The Luxembourg tax authority may levy a fine of up to 10% of the adjusted taxable base and apply interest at 7% per annum.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner is personally and unlimitedly liable for the resulting corporate tax, penalties, and interest. Directors risk disqualification orders and revocation of business permits through the Luxembourg courts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify the ultimate beneficial owners of retainer fees; accepting cash or crypto placement fees from undisclosed principals; failing to file suspicious transaction reports on candidate fee-splitting arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg AML law (Law of 12 November 2004, as amended) imposes administrative fines up to EUR 5,000,000 for serious breaches; criminal money laundering penalties reach 5 years' imprisonment and fines of up to EUR 250,000 per offence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and partners can be sentenced to imprisonment, subject to travel bans, and be ordered to repay laundered amounts. The court may also prohibit them from managing any Luxembourg commercial entity for up to 10 years.
